body:
NIST DLMF section 25.15 (Dirichlet 𝐿-functions) says: "The notation L\left(s,\chiight) was introduced by Dirichlet ( 1837 ) for the meromorphic continuation of the function defined by the series where \chi(n) is a Dirichlet character \pmod{k} (§ 27.8 ). For the principal character \chi_{1}\pmod{k} , L\left(s,\chi_{1}ight) is analytic everywhere except for a simple pole at s=1 with residue \phi\left(kight)/k , where \phi\left(kight) is Euler’s totient function (§ 27.2 ). If \chi
eq\chi_{1} , then L\left(s,\chiight) is an entire function of s . with the product taken over all primes p , beginning with p=2 . This implies that L\left(s,\chiight)
eq 0 if \Re s>1 . Equations ( 25.15.3 ) and ( 25.15.4 ) hold for all s if \chi
eq\chi_{1} , and for all s ( 
eq 1 ) if \chi=\chi_{1} : where \chi_{0} is a primitive character (mod d ) for some positive divisor d of k (§ 27.8 ). When \chi is a primitive character (mod k ) the L -functions satisfy the functional equation:" Equation 25.15.1 on the page has alt text "L\left(s,\chiight)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} rac{\chi(n)}{n^{s}},". Equation 25.15.2 on the page has alt text "L\left(s,\chiight)=\prod_{p}\left(1- rac{\chi(p)}{p^{s}}ight)^{-1},". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
